title: Workshops That Close
intro: Design the workshop backwards from the decision. Open, explore, then close.

learn.title: Three movements
learn.text:
**Open:** generate options.
**Explore:** group, compare, build.
**Close:** choose and commit.

An unsatisfying set of ideas refuses to close.

try.q: Closing fails. Where should you look first?
options: How the space was opened and explored
The voting tool you used and how it was set up

learn.title: Design backwards
learn.text:
Start from the **decision you need**, then pick the opening that feeds it.
Brainstorming opens; affinity mapping explores; voting and ranking close.

learn.title: The $100 test
learn.text:
Groups split an imaginary **$100** across options.

Money holds attention better than points or rankings.

try.q: Why use money in the $100 test?
options: It holds attention better than points
It matches the real budget the team has to spend

learn.title: Five-day sprint
learn.text:
**Mon:** goal, map, target.
**Tue:** sketch alone, recruit.
**Wed:** decide, storyboard.
**Thu:** realistic prototype.
**Fri:** test with customers.

try.q: What happens on Friday of a sprint?
options: Building production code for the chosen idea

test.q: When is a sprint worth running?
options: A critical question before a costly commitment
Every two weeks as a routine part of each cycle
Every view is collected before anchoring
Facilitators prefer a quiet room for the first hour
test.explain: The loudest voice doesn’t set the frame.
